title: Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra (Sanskrit, ed. Sylvain Lévi)
shelf_note: Asaṅga/Maitreya's Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra with bhāṣya, Lévi's edition: core Yogācāra text of the Nālandā curriculum.
structure_note: The scan is two works under one title: Lévi's Sanskrit text (1907; p69 = printed 62) followed by his French translation volume (1911; p248 = printed 27 'LA FAMILLE', p367 = 139, p509 = 279). The 225 printed_repeats and 60 backsteps are the second volume's page numbering restarting, not misreads. The catalogue calls it the Sanskrit edition only (I7); 3 of the 4 sampled pages are French, so the English for most of the book is a translation of Lévi's French, not of the Sanskrit.

book_verdict: A sound Lévi scan, but half of it is the French translation volume while the record calls it the Sanskrit edition. On the Sanskrit page the OCR rewrote Lévi's notes about Chinese renderings into invented Tibetan, and the English stops halfway down the page.
reader_summary: This is Sylvain Lévi's edition of the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra bound with his French translation, so most of the English is translated from Lévi's French rather than from the Sanskrit. The French pages are transcribed accurately and the English follows them well. On the sampled Sanskrit page, though, the footnotes were rewritten (Chinese turned into Tibetan) and the English covers only half the page.

book_verdict: The right text, mostly transcribed well. On sampled pages, misreads change who is speaking (Sāṅkhya read as sādhya), and fluent English covers garbled verse. The book is currently hidden.
reader_summary: This is the Gaekwad's Oriental Series Tattvasaṃgraha with Kamalaśīla's Pañjikā, and the transcription is of the right text. Clean pages such as p491 read accurately. Elsewhere, misreads of names and of the verses carry into confident English, so a specialist should check the Sanskrit before quoting the English.

title: Ratnāvalī (Sanskrit, ed. Mishra & Goswami)
shelf_note: Nāgārjuna's Ratnāvalī, a Madhyamaka work central to the Nālandā tradition.
structure_note: Sanskrit verses each followed by the editors' Hindi rendering, plus a Hindi preface and a verse index (p82, printed 78). The record calls it Sanskrit only. The English mostly translates the Hindi gloss. 81 of 85 pages are translated. The OCR'd page number on p82 reads ७४ for printed ७८.

book_verdict: A modern Hindi-Sanskrit study edition of the Ratnāvalī, probably in copyright. The English renders the Hindi glosses and inverts one verse's meaning.
reader_summary: This is a modern Indian edition of Nāgārjuna's Ratnāvalī with the editors' Hindi translation after each verse. The Sanskrit and Hindi are transcribed well. The English follows the Hindi rather than the Sanskrit and at least once reverses a verse's meaning. The edition is probably still in copyright.

title: Avadana Kalpalata
shelf_note: Kṣemendra's 11th-century Kashmiri verse avadāna collection is Buddhist Sanskrit literature, not a Nālandā śāstra. It is acceptable on a Buddhist-Sanskrit shelf but stretches a Nālandā one.
structure_note: Bibliotheca Indica edition (1888, ed. Sarat Chandra Das and Harimohan Sarma) with Sanskrit and Tibetan on facing pages (p268 is a Tibetan page, 'Sixth pallava'). The record says language Sanskrit. The backsteps are the facing-page numbering pattern, not a defect. 510 of 515 pages are translated.

book_verdict: A solid 1888 bilingual edition, accurately transcribed. The English is sound, apart from model chatter and running-head headings in the reader text. Its shelf is doubtful.
reader_summary: This is the Bibliotheca Indica edition of Kṣemendra's Avadānakalpalatā, with Sanskrit and Tibetan on facing pages. The Sanskrit verse is transcribed accurately and the English follows it closely. The Tibetan pages are serviceable, but one shows the model's own note about the source language at the top of the reader text.
